title: Socca
subtitle: Crispy Provencal chickpea pancake with rosemary and chilli
excerpt: Socca is a thin, blistered pancake from the south of France, made with chickpea flour and olive oil. This version uses plain flour and comes together in minutes. It bakes at high heat and comes out crisp at the edges with a tender, savoury centre. Good as a snack or light starter.
sourceNotes: Inspired by the classic Nice street food socca. Adapted to use plain flour while keeping the high-heat baking technique.

content.text: The baking tray must be very hot before the batter goes on. Put it in the oven while it heats up and leave it there for at least 10 minutes. A cold tray means a pale, soft pancake.
Heat the oven to 230C. Place a large baking tray in the oven to get very hot.
Whisk the flour with 300ml of cold water, 2 tbsp of olive oil, the garlic, and a generous pinch of salt until smooth. The batter should be thin, like single cream.

Carefully remove the hot tray from the oven. Drizzle the remaining olive oil over it. Pour half the batter onto the tray and spread into a thin, even layer. Scatter half the rosemary and chilli flakes over the top.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the edges are crisp and the surface is golden and blistered. Repeat with the remaining batter. Serve in torn pieces, straight from the tray.

items.fix: Preheat the tray for at least 10 minutes next time.
Add a splash more water and whisk again.
